subtitle: PCSX2
_subtitle_source: subtitle names the backend the player will actually run, the same way 18 manifests say "BizHawk".
_platform_source: the world's own README: "This is an implementation for the PS2 version of the game." Its setup guide requires "[PCSX2 emulator]" and "NTSC-U disc or ISO (SCUS-97615)".
_drafted_note: Drafted 2026-08-25 from the world's OWN repository -- its __init__.py, archipelago.json, setup guide and README, read that day. No field is filled in from memory or from what other games on the same console do.
_ap_world_name_source: the world's own archipelago.json: {"game": "Ratchet & Clank: Size Matters"}, read 25 Aug 2026.
description: Ratchet & Clank: Size Matters as a multiworld. Weapons, gadgets, armour pieces and infobots are shuffled across Titanium Bolts, vendors, missions and challenges -- roughly 106 locations on defaults and past 300 with every optional type enabled. Requires the player's own NTSC-U disc (SCUS-97615) and PCSX2 with PINE enabled.
_description_source: written by us from the world's own structure and its setup guide's stated requirements. No text is copied from the game.
_checks_verified_note: FALSE. Nobody has played this. For a kind=world game the checks travel through the WORLD'S client, not through London -- so what is unproven here is not a RAM map of ours (there is none) but the whole chain: apworld installs, emulator starts over the bridge, the world's client attaches and carries a check. London warns at launch while this is false, which is exactly right until a tester reports one.
_requires_source: PS2 title. The setup guide lists it among the player's own requirements: "A copy of Ratchet & Clank: Size Matters -- NTSC-U disc or ISO (SCUS-97615)".

rom.description: Your own Ratchet & Clank: Size Matters disc image for PlayStation 2 -- the NTSC-U release, disc serial SCUS-97615
rom._description_source: the setup guide, word for word: "NTSC-U disc or ISO (`SCUS-97615`)".
rom._hash_note: No hash is claimed. The guide states none.

emulator.name: PCSX2
emulator._source: the setup guide says "[PCSX2 emulator] (2.x or later recommended for the required PINE support)". ⚠ Read as a RECOMMENDATION, not a floor -- the author's own word is "recommended" -- so no minimum is recorded. The PINE requirement itself is stated flatly and is carried in the description instead.

client.name: Ratchet & Clank: Size Matters Client
client._name_source: the world registers it under this exact name in worlds/rac_size_matters/__init__.py. ⚠ Its setup guide abbreviates it to "R&C: Size Matters Client" and the subprocess is named "RACSmClient"; the registered name is what appears in the Archipelago Launcher list, so that is the one recorded.
client._kind_source: the world ships and registers its OWN Archipelago client: worlds/rac_size_matters/__init__.py does `components.append(Component("Ratchet & Clank: Size Matters Client", ..., component_type=Type.CLIENT))` and launches it with launch_subprocess(_run, name="RACSmClient"). The PINE transport is the world's own -- its pypine/ directory, which its README says is adapted from evilwb/pypine. London must NOT read memory for this game.
client._protocol_source: extensions/pcsx2/extension.json declares {"protocol": "pine"}, Systems ["PS2"]. The world carries its own PINE implementation (pypine/) and its setup guide has the player enable PINE in PCSX2.
client._lua_note: No Lua. PINE is spoken to PCSX2 directly.

apworld._source: the author's own releases page; the newest Size Matters release read 25 Aug 2026 is tagged rac-size-matters/v0.4.14, carrying rac_size_matters.apworld. ⚠ The same repository also releases an unrelated dynamicpine.apworld under its own tag -- the Size Matters tag prefix is what identifies this game's build.
apworld._world_version_source: the world's archipelago.json: {"world_version": "0.3.2"}. ⚠ The newest release tag reads v0.4.14, so the world's own file and its tag disagree. Recorded as the world states it, with the difference visible rather than smoothed over.
apworld._minimum_ap_version_source: not stated. The world's archipelago.json carries compatible_version and version but no minimum_ap_version, and the setup guide only says "the latest version of Archipelago". Nothing is claimed.

_patch_extension_source: read from the world's own source, 25 Aug 2026: the 8 .py files at the top of worlds/rac_size_matters were searched. No APPatchExtension, no APProcedurePatch, no patch_file_ending -- this world produces no patch container. ⚠ Scope: its client/, core/ and rules/ subdirectories were not searched; a patch class conventionally lives in the world root, and there is none.
_patch_note: There is deliberately NO `patch` block: the world produces no patch container. The client works on the running game over PINE.

world_by.name: Pangu, Amondo and ImJustATester
world_by._authors_source: the world names them itself: archipelago.json {"authors": ["Pangu", "Amondo", "ImJustATester"]}.
world_by._source: the repository the world is published from; its own source, archipelago.json and setup guide are what this manifest was written against.
world_by._licence_source: the GitHub API reports spdx_id NOASSERTION, name "Other" (25 Aug 2026) -- the repository is an Archipelago fork carrying a licence file GitHub cannot classify. Not read line by line, so nothing more specific is claimed. We redistribute none of this world's code.

credits._game_by_note: Not recorded rather than guessed. The game is the property of its publisher and is never distributed here; the player supplies their own copy. The Archipelago world is its authors' work. Only the plugin itself is by solida1987.

_author_disclosure: The world's own README states: "This is **not** all **Human written code**, this was developed with the help of AI." Recorded because it is the author's own published statement about their world, and a player deciding what to install may want to know. It is not a judgement.
_removal_note: ⚠ Ratchet & Clank 1 and 3 were withdrawn at their author's request (see catalog/removed.json). Size Matters is a different game by a different author (Panguu) and is not on that list; removed.json matches whole titles. The gate in build_plugins.check() was run and is green.
